summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with chronic diastolic heart failure, end-stage renal disease, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for acute shortness of breath and hypoxia. She had been discharged three days prior after an episode of dialysis-related chest pain. This admission was triggered by nocturnal dyspnea, with initial oxygen saturation of 80% at home. In the ED, she had severe hypertension and pulmonary edema on chest X-ray. She was admitted to the ICU, started on nitroglycerin and CPAP, and underwent emergent hemodialysis with removal of 3 liters of fluid, leading to rapid improvement in respiratory status. A mild leukocytosis raised concern for infection, but cultures were negative and antibiotics were discontinued. Her INR was transiently elevated, prompting a temporary hold on warfarin, likely due to antibiotic interaction. Aspirin was reduced to 81 mg daily to reduce bleeding risk. She was weaned to room air, remained hemodynamically stable, and was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with updated medication instructions, sodium restriction, and daily weight monitoring.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
